In C++23, when should std::unique_ptr be preferred?
Prefer std::unique_ptr when exactly one owner controls an object's lifetime. It expresses exclusive ownership, is movable but not copyable, and avoids shared-reference counting overhead.

Why can returning std::string_view to a local std::string be invalid?
The local std::string is destroyed when the function returns. A std::string_view does not own the characters, so the returned view dangles.

What is RAII?
RAII ties resource lifetime to object lifetime: acquire the resource during construction and release it during destruction so cleanup follows scope automatically.

What does std::move actually do?
std::move performs no move itself. It casts its argument to an xvalue, allowing overload resolution to select move operations when available.

When is std::expected useful in C++23?
std::expected is useful when failure is an ordinary, typed outcome and the caller should handle either a value or an error without exceptions.
